source_refs.note: Topic 25.6.3 (PDF 243-244); Figure 25.13 is replaced by an original labelled schematic.

blocks.text: These are high-altitude 'cold deserts' or grasslands where the climate is too harsh for large trees.

blocks.alt: A simple labelled landscape of a alpine and sub-alpine meadows beside an information card.
blocks.caption: The alpine and sub-alpine meadows: a labelled schematic and fact card (original diagram).
blocks.long_description: Snowy peaks above a flowering meadow with a few stunted trees. The card gives the location (Gilgit-Baltistan, Chitral, Swat, AJK, Deosai Plains), climate (mean 1 to 10 C, heavy snow up to 6 feet), plants (stunted junipers, birch, willow, alpine grasses and wild flowers), animals (snow leopard, Himalayan brown bear, ibex, musk deer, marmot, monal, golden eagle) and status (fragile and sensitive to warming).

blocks.caption: Profile of the alpine and sub-alpine meadows
rows: mountain tops of Gilgit-Baltistan, Chitral, Swat, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and the Deosai Plains
severe cold; mean annual 1 to 10 C
mostly heavy snow, up to 6 feet
stunted junipers, birch (Betula utilis), willow, alpine grasses and wild flowers
snow leopard, Himalayan brown bear, Himalayan ibex, musk deer, marmots; snowcock, monal, golden eagle
fragile: very sensitive to global warming, as melting snow upsets the meadow's balance

blocks.prompt: Name one plant and one animal of the alpine and sub-alpine meadows.
blocks.explanation: For example stunted junipers and snow leopard.

items: Alpine and sub-alpine meadows: mountain tops of Gilgit-Baltistan, Chitral, Swat, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, and the Deosai Plains.
Status: fragile: very sensitive to global warming, as melting snow upsets the meadow's balance.
